digest.component_or_area: Bridge tracker-sync CLI and library surface
propositions: Bridge redesign unifies fragmented Jira-specific operator surface into a single provider-neutral, Python-first command surface (rebar bridge) while retaining legacy reconcile and bridge-status compatibility.

Canonical verbs (setup, check-access, fsck, status, preview, sync, pause, resume) and exit codes (0, 1, 2) are stable; legacy adapters translate historical codes (3, 4, 75) and reconcile remains non-mutating by default while bridge sync is mutating.

Python library, CLI, and MCP server expose identical bridge operations through shared core; pip, Homebrew, and MCP installation paths execute the same implementation without editable checkouts or repository-only helpers.
Pause state is durably persisted with reason metadata, readable by mixed-version fleets, and destructive repair operations no longer require GitHub gh CLI.
Bridge execution is runner-neutral across local, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, and bare environments with shared code-derived exit behavior, secrets vocabulary, and timeout policy.

Tickets-branch delivery (CAS retry, fetch-and-merge recovery, strict failure classification) is owned by Python core (src/rebar/_store/push.py) with no workflow-local retry loops; all 20 descendants merged, ADR 0092 indexed, and all acceptance criteria completed at commit 694cf894def36241724e7049e3308d782037ef6d.
